Khandu has convened the meeting with representatives of the ABK Youth Wing and the Adi Students' Union. However, the Siang Indigenous Farmers' Forum Youth Wing has called for a boycott until four key demands were fulfilled. Accusing the state government of adopting a high-handed approach towards indigenous communities opposing the project, SIFFYW said there should be no dialogue unless FIRs against villagers and activists involved in anti-dam protests and Central Armed Police Forces deployed in the Siang region are withdrawn. It also demanded immediate and safe release of all currently in police or judicial custody, full compensation for injured villagers and restitution for damage to private vehicles and village properties. SIFFYW called upon community organisations, student unions, clan representatives and political leaders to refrain from engaging with the government over the Siang Upper Multipurpose Project under the guise of consultations. It asserted that there cannot be any dialogue while protesters were behind bars and their grievances were not resolved. Anti-dam activist and SIFFYW legal advisor Ebo Mili said, "What's the point of them meeting with the chief minister? No one can decide the future of the entire Adi community unless the CF is withdrawn.. He maintained that the chief minister was free to meet any Adi organisation, community-based organisation or student union on other issues but not SUMP. The hydropower project has been facing opposition from locals of the Siang region, over concerns about a possible impact on their traditional way of life amid fears over displacement, ecological damage and the risks associated with building a mega project in a seismically active region. news.headline: Adhikari launches Durga Puja festivities, cites adherence to religious norms

That’s why it is being launched today, as the Devi Paksha has begun.
news.full_article_text: Adhikari launches Durga Puja festivities, cites adherence to religious norms This is the first Durga Puja since the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) came to power in May this year, ousting the Trinamool Congress government West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari on Saturday launched the festivities centred around this year’s Durga Puja, the biggest festival for people in the eastern state, at a grand ceremony at the Netaji Indoor Stadium in Kolkata. “Our government decided that the Durga Puja (festivities) cannot be initiated during the Pitru Paksha phase. That’s why it is being launched today, as the Devi Paksha has begun. On one hand, we decided to maintain the cultural tradition of the Durga Puja; on the other hand, we decided to adhere to the religious norms and our scriptures,” he said. This is the first Durga Puja since the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) came to power in May this year, ousting the Trinamool Congress government. Former CM Mamata Banerjee faced criticism in 2025 from the opposition and some religious and Hindu rights organisations for inaugurating puja pandals before Mahalaya, which marks the transition from Pitru Paksha to Devi Paksha. “Till last year, around 45,000 community pujas were organised by various clubs and organisations across the state. This year, the number has jumped by around 12,400. Earlier, people had to approach the Calcutta high court to seek permission to organise Durga Puja. This year, there has been no such instance to my knowledge,” Adhikari said while addressing the programme, which was attended by an audience of around 40,000. West Bengal governor RN Ravi, ministers, senior bureaucrats and leaders from various spiritual organisations attended the programme. Exiled Bangladeshi author Taslima Nasreen also attended the event. The dignitaries first attended a roadshow led by Adhikari and then attended the grand ceremony. Apart from the cultural programmes, at least 3,000 drones lit up the sky over the stadium, depicting Goddess Durga and scenes including the traditional Dhunuchi Naach. The state tourism department and the information and cultural affairs department will organise special cultural programmes in various cities and tourist destinations, including one on Digha beach, over the next four days before the main Puja celebrations begin. The new BJP government in the state had earlier reduced the grant for Durga Puja committees from 110,000 provided last year by the previous Mamata Banerjee-led government to ₹ 100,000 this year. It also announced a complete ban on DJs during the festivities and the closure of liquor outlets and bars on Maha Ashtami. The Durga Puja carnival, a pet project of Banerjee, has also been cancelled this year.

The Delhi Police on Saturday issued a clarification after purported videos on social media showed police officials allegedly enter the premises of Gurdwara Bangla Sahib wearing shoes. The police clarified that the officials were “walking in the common passage” which was used by all devotees to reach the entry point of the Gurdwara.

Sharing a video of the Bangla Sahib, the Delhi Police said the passage led to the point where shoes were taken off before entering the place of worship. “The process is the same for all devotees coming to Gurdwara. The video showing the same is attached,” it clarified.
The Delhi Police alleged that the video circulated on social media had “malicious intent” and was aimed at “outraging the feelings of a respectable religious community”.
The police said that legal action was being initiated against those circulating the video showing the cops in bad light.
The video came as Delhi Police teams were deployed outside the Gurdwara to nab protesters taking part in the anti-CEC agitation called by the Cockroach Janta Party on October 10.

The Delhi Police on Saturday launched a massive crackdown across the city and detained over 4,000 people in view of the anti-CEC stir and CJP's call for march to Jantar Mantar. As police personnel moved to take him away, party workers tried to prevent his detention. Police personnel lifted him by his legs and chest and carried him towards a police bus. Those party leaders detained with him included Rajya Sabha member Sanjay Singh, Delhi unit chief Saurabh Bharadwaj, MLA Kuldeep Kumar and national media in-charge Anurag Dhanda. Senior AAP leader Gopal Rai was also detained while protesting at the party office. "... Till now, Modi ji used to win elections only by stealing votes. Now he has been caught red-handed," he said. "Wherever Modi ji stops you, sit there. Turn that place into Jantar Mantar. Now CEC Gyanesh Kumar has to resign. People are not going to tolerate his vote theft anymore." Banerjee was detained along with Trinamool Congress leaders from South Avenue, where they staged a sit-in after being stopped from proceeding to Jantar Mantar. Banerjee, accompanied by TMC leaders Derek O'Brien, Dola Sen, Samirul Islam, Pratima Mondal and Saket Gokhale, wore a band-aid over her mouth during the protest. Vijayan was detained along with Sarkar, Baby and Karat as they attempted to proceed to Jantar Mantar. "Amit Shah, dekho hum Jantar Mantar aa gaye," Karat told PTI, describing the slogans raised by the protesters. More than a lakh students, one lakh students have registered on the online QR code registration,” Tagore said. "Without a QR code, we are not going to allow anybody. And there are restrictions we have put on those selection processes also, who are going to be the students who are going to be entering here," the Congress MP added. news.story_lead: Delhi protest: Right-wing groups assault protesters, journalists amid heavy security deployment Many of the men were seen beating protesters in front of police personnel, including instances at Connaught Place that unfolded in front of HT reporters. Groups of men from right-wing organisations threatened and assaulted protesters and journalists in Connaught Place and near the MCD Civic Centre on Saturday, even as more than 25,000 security personnel held the centre of the Capital against the protest. news.full_article_text: Delhi protest: Right-wing groups assault protesters, journalists amid heavy security deployment Many of the men were seen beating protesters in front of police personnel, including instances at Connaught Place that unfolded in front of HT reporters. Groups of men from right-wing organisations threatened and assaulted protesters and journalists in Connaught Place and near the MCD Civic Centre on Saturday, even as more than 25,000 security personnel held the centre of the Capital against the protest. "You all are showing fake news for CJP. We will protect Delhi Police since they can't use arms against you," one of them shouted. Police chased the men away and detained some of them half an hour later. Deep Dive Near the MCD Civic Centre, a confrontation between protesters and men from the Hindustan Raksha Dal turned violent when the men began dragging, assaulting and threatening women and men on the street. Also Read | CJP asks ‘where is Abhijeet’ after Delhi Police say Dipke was informed of grandmother’s death In one video of an assault at the location, which spread widely on social media within hours, protesters were seen being slapped, kicked and assaulted. The video, which HT has not verified, showed a young woman being dragged and beaten by two men until her sister pulls her away. "Nobody came to save me. Delhi police saw everything," the woman says in the video. Senior Delhi Police officers said police had rescued the woman, helped her and removed the men from the spot. No FIR has been filed against the men at the time of reporting. HT reached out to the Bajrang Dal, several Delhi Police spokespersons and the deputy commissioner of police (New Delhi), but received no response. In another video, purportedly shot near Connaught Place, men attack a protester with brass knuckles and tear his T-shirt. A 21-year-old media student from Shahdara, who was hiding at Gurdwara Bangla Sahib and declined to be named, said he and two friends had been targeted by both the police and the men. "My two friends and I have been facing assault because of police as well as these right wing goons. They entered the protest not once but thrice since last night. Police didn't even stop them. They hit my friend on the head but he managed to escape. We were making videos as we are media students. But they threatened to beat us and hurled abuses. We left in fear," he said. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Jignasa Sinha Jignasa Sinha is a Special Correspondent at Hindustan Times in New Delhi. India has rejected the UN Human Rights Office’s (OHCHR) remarks on the events in New Delhi, calling its concerns “misplaced” and accusing it of unwarranted interference in the country’s internal affairs. In a statement shared by the Permanent Mission of India to the UN in Geneva on X, India said the right to peaceful assembly was guaranteed by the Constitution and safeguarded by the country’s institutions, an independent judiciary and a free media. “We have seen the OHCHR’s remarks about today’s events in New Delhi,” the mission said, adding that citizens exercise their right to peaceful assembly subject to reasonable restrictions in the interest of public order. India also called on the OHCHR to devote comparable attention to large-scale protests elsewhere, arguing that the UN body should act in keeping with its mandate of impartiality and non-selectivity. UN raises concerns over Delhi detentions The response came after the United Nations expressed concern over mass detentions in Delhi amid protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The demonstrations have been accompanied by heightened security measures and restrictions in parts of the national capital. The protests, called by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and other groups, are linked to demands for Kumar’s resignation over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Delhi Police denied permission for the CJP’s proposed October 10 demonstration at Jantar Mantar, citing short notice, alleged violations during earlier protests and concerns over public safety, traffic and law and order. The restrictions triggered legal scrutiny, with the Supreme Court intervening over curbs affecting public transport and calling for a balance between the right to protest and the need to prevent disruption to essential services. In their letter to the citizens of India, the 124 former IAS, IFS and allied services officers said the country’s electoral system had undergone a significant transformation from the era of booth capturing, ballot box stuffing and election-related violence. They highlighted safeguards such as polling agents, the sealing of electronic voting machines (EVMs), strong-room security and Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail (VVPAT) verification. Also Read | Delhi protest: Right-wing groups assault protesters, journalists amid heavy security deployment The letter comes amid protests in Delhi and Mumbai against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over allegations of electoral irregularities. “A system cannot be honest when you win and rigged when you lose,” the letter stated, according to ANI, noting that the party ruling at the Centre had lost several state elections under the same Election Commission. The officers also referred to the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, in which the ruling party failed to secure an outright majority on its own. Defending the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise, the former civil servants described it as a necessary process to maintain accurate electoral rolls by identifying deceased voters, duplicate entries and individuals who had permanently shifted residence. Also Read | 'EC at centre of assault': 42 ex-judges defend India's poll process in open letter amid protest against Gyanesh Kumar They also maintained that the SIR process included safeguards to address concerns over wrongful exclusion, including the publication of draft electoral rolls, opportunities to file claims and objections, hearings and provisions for appeals. “Questioning is every citizen’s right. Proving is the accuser’s duty,” the officers said, adding that unsubstantiated allegations could weaken public confidence in democratic institutions and the electoral process. news.full_article_text: A blast was heard at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh - Published 10 October 2026, 16:05 BST Several people have been injured in another attack on an international airport in the Saudi capital Riyadh, authorities say, days after Yemen's Houthis claimed to have carried out similar strikes on the hub. Operations at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh were suspended on Saturday after the attack, the Saudi Civil Aviation Authority said in a statement. More than a dozen ambulances were seen rushing to the airport, according to news agency Reuters, citing an eyewitness. The US embassy said it was "aware of attacks on King Khalid International Airport" and urged American citizens to avoid the airport and surrounding areas. The attack comes a day after authorities said three Saudis including a pilot were killed in two attacks on the airport by the Iran-backed Houthis the day prior. Another three people were killed in Houthi attacks on two Saudi airports on 6 and 7 October. A source at a local hospital told AFP that dozens of people had been wounded in Saturday's attack. "I saw 401 hit, I saw injured in front of my eyes. Everyone was running," an eyewitness who said they had been at gate 401 in the domestic terminal told the news agency. Western embassies in Saudi Arabia have warned their citizens away from the airport, while the UK Foreign Office told British nationals to stay away "until the airport is secure and to monitor the advice of the Saudi authorities". Several Gulf airlines said they had cancelled their flights to and from the airport, with Kuwait Airways citing the "security situation" there. All flights to Riyadh have either been diverted or cancelled, aviation tracker Flightradar shows. Doctors had been asked to report to hospitals to address the situation, a medical source told AFP. "We were told we are dealing with a 'serious emergency situation'," the medical source told the agency. The suspected attack comes during a marked escalation in renewed fighting between Yemen's Saudi-backed government forces and the Houthis, who control most of the country's north-west. The Houthis say they are targeting Saudi Arabia over its support for government forces in Yemen's civil war. The conflict worsened after the Houthis seized strategically important stretches of the Red Sea coast in a rapid offensive. That included the port of Mokha on the Bab al-Mandab Strait, which is the narrowest point of the Red Sea and a chokepoint for global shipping. Yemeni pro-government forces have since said they had "secured" the strait at the southern end of the Red Sea. A Saudi-led coalition was formed in 2015 after Arab countries joined forces to stop the Houthis taking over Yemen from the country's internationally recognised government. A temporary ceasefire was brokered in 2022 after years of air strikes and ground fighting led to the deaths of hundreds of thousands of people, triggering one of the world's worst humanitarian crises. But the informal truce began to unravel in July. The Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea. They said they were retaliating against what they described as a years-long Saudi blockade and for an air strike on Sanaa airport. The order, dated October 9 and approved by Union home secretary Govind Mohan, suspended mobile internet within 500 metres of each site from noon to 10pm on Saturday. "It is necessary and expedient so to do in the interest of public order and for preventing incitement to the commission of any offence," it said. news.headline: 'Time for Ukraine to get new president,' says Trump after Zelensky condemns diesel deal
news.story_lead: Watch: 'Time for Ukraine to get a new president', says Trump - Published 10 October 2026, 18:31 BST US President Donald Trump has said he thinks "it's time for Ukraine to get a new president" as he responded to Volodymyr Zelensky's criticism of the US diesel deal with Russia. The Ukrainian president warned a new deal to release millions of tonnes of Russian diesel into the US would provide Moscow with money to continue its war against his nation, calling it a gift to Russian President Vladimir Putin. Trump told reporters outside the White House on Saturday that Zelensky "wants to make problems for the world" by continuing to authorise attacks on Russian refineries.
news.full_article_text: Watch: 'Time for Ukraine to get a new president', says Trump - Published 10 October 2026, 18:31 BST US President Donald Trump has said he thinks "it's time for Ukraine to get a new president" as he responded to Volodymyr Zelensky's criticism of the US diesel deal with Russia. The Ukrainian president warned a new deal to release millions of tonnes of Russian diesel into the US would provide Moscow with money to continue its war against his nation, calling it a gift to Russian President Vladimir Putin. Trump told reporters outside the White House on Saturday that Zelensky "wants to make problems for the world" by continuing to authorise attacks on Russian refineries. "He'd better damn well stop," Trump said, before suggesting Ukraine should "get a new leader who can make a deal". Russia and Ukraine have recently intensified their strikes, targeting energy-generating and transport facilities, as well as major logistics hubs. "We said, 'you can do whatever you want to Russia, don't hit the refineries', because that's a world problem that's caused," he said. "He could have made many deals and for some reason, he never does." Putin's envoy Kirill Dmitriev described Trump's intervention as "iconic and historic", saying that Ukraine "needs leadership actually focused on peace". The US president confirmed on Friday that an agreement had been reached with Moscow to suspend sanctions on Russian diesel exports until 7 April. Zelensky reacted by saying it would allow Moscow to raise new funds to source new military equipment to continue the war. He also accused Moscow of taking the deal "to mean they can keep fighting, to mean they keep dropping bombs on cities" following deadly new strikes on Zaporizhzhia. - Analysis: Trump's shock Russia deal highlights mounting pressure to curb fuel prices Published 20 hours ago The Ukrainian president spoke to several allies on Saturday to discuss the latest developments, calling for "real decisions to protect lives in Ukraine" and to protect European security. A Downing Street spokesperson said UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham had spoken to Zelensky and that the pair had agreed Russia should acquiesce to "an immediate energy ceasefire" and end its attacks on shipping in the Black Sea. "This would immediately release more energy and food supplies into the global market," the spokesperson added. News of the US-Russia diesel deal was also met with criticism by EU's foreign affairs chief Kaja Kallas, who echoed Zelensky in saying that suspending sanctions "provides Moscow with more revenues to wage war", adding: "This is not the time to ease pressure on Russia, and Europe won't." She said European foreign ministers intended to approve the biggest set of sanctions on Russia since the start of its full-scale invasion on Monday. The deal with Russia is the latest effort from Trump to lower fuel prices in the US ahead of the midterm elections, after months spent grappling with the political consequences of the Iran war. That conflict, which began in February, has sent the cost of petrol and in particular diesel skyrocketing, which has soured his standing with the American public who have been stung by the higher pump prices and knock-on effects that led to across-the-board inflation. The average price of diesel is currently $6.28 (Â£4.74) a gallon, according to the AAA â up from last month's $5.94 average, and $3.68 last year. Under the deal, Russia would release an initial 300,000 tonnes of diesel "to the American and global marketplace" followed by an additional 500,000 tonnes in November. A further million would follow, Trump wrote on Truth Social, and then another 3m tonnes "within a short period of time" â but he noted that this delivery will be "based on the condition of their diesel refineries". In the past 10 months, Russia experienced two waves of severe fuel shortages across the country due to Ukrainian drones strikes on its oil refineries. Diesel production in Russia dropped by an estimated 30%, according to the International Energy Agency. Trump had already called for new elections in Ukraine last December , external , saying Ukrainian voters should have the choice to replace Zelensky. Since the war broke out in 2022 Ukraine has been under martial law, meaning elections are suspended. news.full_article_text: Supreme Court to hear on Sunday pleas against violation of order on Delhi curbs, detention of Opposition leaders A special Bench comprising Justices Bagchi and Mohana will hear the matter. The plea alleges that authorities failed to comply with the court’s directions Trinamool Congress MP and senior advocate Menaka Guruswamy has moved the Supreme Court challenging the preventive detention of Opposition leaders, including four former chief ministers, and other individuals during Saturday’s protests in Delhi against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar , prompting a special sitting of the court on Sunday. A bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana will hear the matter on October 11, along with a separate contempt petition alleging that authorities failed to comply with the Supreme Court ’s Friday order against a blanket shutdown of Metro and railway services ahead of the demonstrations. Track live updates from Delhi protests TMC MP questions detention of protestors, Oppn leaders Guruswamy has questioned the police action of picking up protesters from the streets and Opposition leaders from their residences, arguing that preventive detention cannot be used to suppress the fundamental right to peaceful protest, particularly when it involves political leaders who have previously governed states. The petition follows Saturday’s crackdown on a protest called by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and other political groups at Jantar Mantar, demanding Kumar’s resignation over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. Delhi Police had denied permission for the demonstration, citing security considerations. The court will also consider a contempt plea filed by advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi against Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan, Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar and Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) chairperson D Thara, alleging that the authorities failed to implement its October 9 directions on public transport and traffic management. Also Read | 'Don't use hammer to kill a fly': Supreme Court asks Centre, Delhi Police to lift blanket curbs on metro, trains The petition, filed through advocate Chand Qureshi, contends that despite the Supreme Court’s order requiring the authorities to ensure that commuters were not inconvenienced, 57 Metro stations remained subject to closure restrictions, several trains scheduled to arrive at or depart from New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin stations were cancelled, and no traffic advisory was published in newspapers. Also Read | INDIA bloc to hold mega protest in Delhi on October 12, TMC says Mamata Banerjee to join “Notwithstanding the solemn judicial mandate and the assurance recorded before the bench of the Chief Justice of India (CJI), the contemnors have consciously maintained a blanket shutdown across transit corridors, persisted with unwarranted train cancellations, and failed to issue or publicize transparent traffic and transit advisories,” the contempt plea said. It alleged that the measures had severely disrupted public life in the national capital, stranded essential travellers and amounted to a deliberate attempt to undermine the authority of the court. What order did SC pass on curbs on Friday? The contempt proceedings arise from Friday’s hearing before a bench headed by CJI Surya Kant, along with Justices Bagchi and V Mohana, on a petition filed by CPI(M) general secretary MA Baby challenging the sweeping restrictions imposed ahead of Saturday’s proposed protest. Senior advocates Kapil Sibal, Abhishek Manu Singhvi and Gopal Sankaranarayanan had told the court that the restrictions, including Metro station closures, train cancellations and extensive road barricading, would cause disproportionate hardship to ordinary residents who depended on public transport to commute to work, attend educational institutions and access essential services. Also Read | 'Will come back stronger': CJP's Ajinkya Shinde calls fresh protest after Delhi Police crackdown on Jantar Mantar stir The bench questioned the rationale for a blanket shutdown, emphasising that security concerns could justify regulating public transport but not bringing the entire system to a halt. “Stopping something and regulating are two different concepts. One can regulate but it is completely different to put a halt on everything…you cannot stop everything,” the bench observed, adding that authorities could not use a “hammer to kill a fly”. In its order, the court clarified that there should be no outright prohibition on Metro services and that authorities could allow Metro trains and other rail services to operate in a suitable and regulated manner. It also directed that traffic advisories be published in newspapers and on online platforms to ensure that commuters faced no hardship while travelling within the city. The court directed the authorities to give wide publicity to their decisions and ordered the DMRC, the relevant railway authorities and Delhi Police’s traffic wing to file a compliance report within four days.
